I worked in a lumber mill in my early 20s. The industry standards were 1 3/4 x 3 3/4. Got a huge shipment sent back to us from some part of China because they thought we were ripping them off because our 2x4's weren't actually 2x4's.
I did demo on my parents' house when they were remodeling and it was so old it had real 2x4s. It blew my mind. They seemed so thick. Of course modifications had to be made to fit the new 2x4s in.

I do home renovations and run into from time to time. What I find funny is that I can find better quality lumber in a 100 year old house than I ever would in any house from the past 60 years.

Last employer is doing a job on an old heritage house (about 120 years old), and I was amazed to see how little those old 2x4's bowed or flexed over such a long period of time. The ceiling rafters were immaculate. It was a real treat.

LOL, they also had the original steel tub in the bathroom as the door was tiny compared to the tub.
